title: From Images to Insight: Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSSs) in Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology.
desc: [Kathmandu University medical journal (KUMJ)] The clinician's preliminary diagnosis and the pathologist's conclusive histopathological diagnosis, which is considered the gold standard, are not always the same. Due to time constraints and the high volume of patients, clinicians often rely on initial impressions or memorable experiences, which can potentially lead to diagnostic inaccuracies. Artificial Intelligence (AI), with its data-driven approach, offers a more objective analysis free from personal biases. Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSSs), combine demographic, clinical, and radiological data, to generate differential diagnoses, providing clinicians with additional decision support. This, in turn, increases the efficiency and accuracy of clinical diagnoses. CDSSs have demonstrated high accuracy rates in internal medicine, especially when diagnosing common chief complaints. Bayesian Belief Networks (BBNs) are applied in both medical and dental fields to enhance diagnostic accuracy. An example is the Oral Radiographic Differential Diagnosis (ORADIII) system developed by the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) in the 1990s, which employs the Bayesian approach to diagnose intra-bony lesions of the jaw. Using AI in decision support for diagnosing bony jaw lesions (including cysts and tumors) lies in its potential to aid in improving clinician's diagnostic accuracy, efficiency, and consistency. AI can further help with complex diagnoses, reduce diagnostic errors, provide support in high-volume or remote settings, as well as work educational tool for students.

title: DeepOSSA: a deep learning framework for personalized survival prediction in osteosarcoma patients.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
desc: [Frontiers in cell and developmental biology] Osteosarcoma, the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, is marked by high invasiveness and heterogeneous outcomes due to inter-patient variability in tumor biology and treatment response. Accurate prognostic modeling is crucial for personalized risk stratification and clinical decision-making. We developed and validated DeepOSSA, a deep learning framework for individualized survival prediction in osteosarcoma, leveraging high-dimensional, sparsely encoded clinical data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Clinical data from 895 osteosarcoma patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were extracted. Continuous variables were optimally discretized using X-tile, and categorical covariates were one-hot encoded. We compared DeepOSSA against seven representative models spanning classical machine learning (support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT)), deep learning (multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and Transformer), and survival analysis (Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) and DeepSurv). DeepOSSA integrates a Transformer-based representation tower for high-order sparse feature crossing with a Cox-style discrete-time survival head, enabling joint optimization of feature representation and time-to-event modeling. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using the area under the curve (AUC) and F1-score. DeepOSSA outperformed all baselines in discrimination and balanced classification, achieving an AUC of 0.8058 ± 0.0081 and an F1-score of 0.6506 ± 0.0060 , representing average relative improvements of 13.11% (AUC) and 8.99% (F1), respectively. Among all evaluated models, DeepOSSA achieved the highest AUC (exceeding 0.8) and demonstrated competitive performance compared with previously published, externally validated Cox nomograms for osteosarcoma. In time-dependent evaluation, its predictive advantage over CoxPH increased during long-term follow-up, where proportional hazards assumptions are most violated. Ablation studies confirmed the necessity of each architectural component, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis demonstrated that the model's risk predictions are driven by clinically established prognostic factors. By capturing attention-based nonlinear interactions and temporal dynamics, DeepOSSA enables more precise patient stratification than traditional linear models. AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.
desc: [European radiology] To evaluate the potential of BoneView, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for fracture detection on radiographs in claims cases related to missed fractures that resulted in financial compensation. This retrospective, multicenter study included all patients who submitted a claim and received financial compensation for missed fractures on radiographs between January 2013 and December 2019 across the 38 university hospitals of the Greater Paris area (AP-HP-France). For each claimant, 5 control patients were selected from a contemporary single-center cohort of patients who underwent radiographs of the same anatomical regions (with or without fracture) performed in the emergency department of a university hospital, irrespective of fracture status. Three radiologists (musculoskeletal fellow, 5-year fellowship-trained radiologist, and > 20-year expert) independently performed blinded, unassisted, and AI-assisted interpretations following a 3-month washout. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated with and without AI and for standalone AI. Compensation amounts were used to estimate potentially avoidable payouts. 156 patients (mean age, 42.2 years; 113 (72.4%) males), including 26 claimants with missed fractures on radiographs and 130 controls, were evaluated. 27/130 (20.8%) of the control cohort had fractures. Standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% (21/26; 95% CI [60.7-93.5]) for claimants and 96.3% (26/27; 95% CI [81.0-99.9]) for the control cohort (p = 0.10). AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10). Total compensation was €282,850 (€10,878 per case). AI-assisted detection could have potentially mitigated €265,314, representing a 93.8% theoretical reduction in institutional financial liability. AI-assisted fracture detection identified most missed fractures on radiographs leading to compensation and may help reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Question Can AI-assisted fracture detection identify fractures missed by radiologists on radiographs that led to compensated medicolegal claims and institutional financial liability? Findings Standalone AI detected 21/26 (80.8%) of missed fractures in patients with compensated claims, corresponding to €265,314/€282,850 (93.8%) of total compensation in this cohort. [Being attentive to sarcopenia in elderly patients with refractory wounds].
source: PubMed · Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi
desc: [Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi] Sarcopenia is a major threat to the health of elderly patients. Elderly patients with refractory wounds are at increased risk of sarcopenia and have poorer outcomes, however, its clinical recognition and management remain inadequate. Based on an understanding of the bidirectional deterioration between sarcopenia and refractory wounds, healthcare professionals should draw on relevant consensus and guidelines, incorporate sarcopenia into routine screening, comprehensive assessment, and dynamic re-assessment, and provide integrated management encompassing nutritional support and metabolic regulation, immune and inflammatory modulation, wound care, physical activity and rehabilitation, and psychological support. Future research and clinical practice, supported by technologies such as artificial intelligence and multi-omics, will be conducted to establish consensus on screening, diagnosis, and treatment for sarcopenia in elderly patients with refractory wounds, thereby improving their clinical outcomes and quality of life.

Multidimensional linguistic evaluation of LLM-generated and resident-rewritten discharge summaries.
source: PubMed · International journal of medical informatics
desc: [International journal of medical informatics] Clinical documentation frequently involves complex terminology and dense information that challenges plain language communication during care transitions. Large Language Models (LLM) have increasingly been used to generate easier-to-understand medical texts, although multidimensional linguistic evaluations of their outputs remain limited. This study compared GPT-5-generated and resident-rewritten versions of hospital discharge summaries in producing patient-friendly language. Discharge summaries were randomly allocated to medical residents in training programs for rewriting and were also rewritten by GPT-5, an OpenAI model. These summaries were evaluated for readability and textual comprehensibility using quantitative linguistic metrics across lexical, semantic, cohesion, and discourse domains. Prompt instructions were standardized through prompt engineering procedures. Pairwise comparisons were performed via the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and Spearman correlation coefficients were used to examine associations across linguistic variables. Fifty-nine paired discharge summaries were analyzed. LLM-generated texts demonstrated greater readability and lexical simplification, stronger referential cohesion and greater textual predictability with more familiar and imageable vocabulary. Conversely, resident-rewritten discharge summaries presented greater informational density with lower semantic ambiguity and higher lexical diversity. Overall syntactic complexity remained similar between groups. Correlation analyses suggested a more clustered, domain-segregated pattern of associations in LLM outputs, whereas resident-rewritten summaries showed associations spanning a broader range of linguistic domains. The evaluated LLM improved discharge-summary readability and accessibility, whereas resident-rewritten summaries preserved greater semantic specificity and informational density. Human oversight and validation with patients remain essential to ensure clinically reliable simplification of patient-facing discharge documents.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) anxiety and nurses' turnover intention during healthcare digital transformation: the mediating role of occupational fatigue.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare is associated with new psychological challenges. However, the extent of its impact on nursing workforce stability is unclear. To explore the relationship between AI anxiety and turnover intention of clinical nurses, and the mediating effect of occupational fatigue and the moderating effect of emotional intelligence (EI). A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2026 among 404 clinical nurses from four hospitals in Jiangsu Province, China. Data were collected using the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS), Health Workers' Occupational Fatigue Scale (HWOFS), Turnover Intention Scale (TIS) and Wong and Law Emotional Intelligence Scale (WLEIS). Mediation was tested using structural equation modelling with bootstrap resampling, while moderation was tested using moderated regression analysis. Differences in baseline turnover intentions across age, department, and professional title level were statistically significant (all p < 0.001). Path analysis showed that AI anxiety was positively associated with occupational fatigue (β = 0.611, p < 0.001) and turnover intention (β = 0.530, p < 0.001). Occupational fatigue partially mediated the association between AI anxiety and turnover intention (indirect effect = 0.299, 95% CI: 0.129, 0.379). EI had a significant negative main effect on occupational fatigue (b = -0.257, p < 0.001), but it did not significantly moderate the association between AI anxiety and occupational fatigue. AI anxiety is significantly correlated with the turnover intention of clinical nurses, and occupational fatigue may represent a potential pathway linking AI anxiety and turnover intention. Although EI is associated with lower levels of occupational fatigue, it fails to cushion the impact of AI anxiety, a specific stressor. Hospital administrators should focus on targeted AI literacy improvement plans and specific fatigue relief strategies to retain clinical nursing staff.

title: Biological state-guided oncology: a framework for dynamic precision cancer care through oncological state transitions.
source: PubMed · Expert review of anticancer therapy
desc: [Expert review of anticancer therapy] Precision oncology has transformed cancer treatment through molecular profiling, but clinical decisions remain largely anchored to baseline assessments that incompletely capture evolving tumor biology and host conditions. This review proposes the Oncological State Transition (OST) framework as a conceptual approach to cancer as a dynamic process of evolving tumor and host biological states. We examine the biological basis of state transitions and the potential roles of longitudinal liquid biopsy, multi-omics, functional imaging, digital pathology, artificial intelligence, and digital twins in multimodal state assessment. Potential applications across prevention, surgery, systemic therapy, minimal residual disease surveillance, therapeutic resistance, and survivorship are discussed, together with challenges in clinical validation and implementation. OST provides a testable framework for integrating longitudinal multimodal information to estimate current biological states and potential future transitions. It emphasizes probabilistic state estimation and the distinction between biological and actionable transitions. Rather than replacing conventional staging or molecular classification, OST may complement precision oncology by supporting dynamic state assessment and adaptive decision-making. Prospective studies and randomized comparisons are required to establish its clinical utility. OST therefore represents a potential foundation for Dynamic Precision Oncology, but remains a conceptual framework rather than a validated clinical system.

title: MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram for differentiating FIGO 2023 stage I from stage II-IV endometrial cancer: a multicenter study.
desc: [Insights into imaging] Preoperative identification of FIGO 2023 stage I endometrial cancer (EC) is important for treatment planning. We aimed to develop and validate a deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) based on multiparametric MRI to distinguish stage I EC from stage II-IV disease. This study retrospectively enrolled patients from three centers. Patients from Centers 1 and 2 were randomly split into a training set (n = 616), and an internal test set (n = 158), and Center 3 served as an external test set (n = 232). The DLRN integrated deep-learning features, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical characteristics. The DLRN was compared with clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning models. Discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with AUCs compared using DeLong's test. A total of 1006 patients (mean age, 56.5 ± 9.7 years) were analyzed. In the internal test set, the DLRN achieved an AUC of 0.852, higher than the clinical (0.673; p = 0.001), original radiomics (0.765; p = 0.030), and combined radiomics (0.793; p = 0.050) models. In the external test set, the DLRN remained robust (AUC = 0.829) and outperformed the clinical, original radiomics, and combined radiomics models (AUC = 0.680, 0.681, and 0.743; all p < 0.005). With DLRN assistance, radiologists showed improved diagnostic performance. The MRI-based DLRN showed robust discrimination between FIGO 2023 stage I and stage II-IV EC across test sets, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification and decision support. Question The introduction of the FIGO 2023 staging system has made the differentiation between stages more challenging, highlighting the need for better tools. Findings A new MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) accurately identifies high-risk patients, significantly outperforming traditional and individual clinical prediction methods. Critical relevance statement This tool helps doctors make better preoperative treatment plans, potentially improving patient outcomes in endometrial cancer.

title: A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics.
desc: [Journal of dentistry] To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI. Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability. AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence. The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.

title: Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema: Current Status and Future Perspective.
desc: [The clinical respiratory journal] Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) is a clinical syndrome defined by the coexistence of upper-lobe emphysema and lower-lobe pulmonary fibrosis. It is characterized by clinical, functional, and radiologic features that differ significantly from isolated idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This review summarizes recent advances in CPFE, focusing on etiologic classification, clinical and radiologic features, diagnosis and treatment, prognostic evaluation, and emerging perspectives in artificial intelligence (AI). Based on current research, we summarize the etiologic classification of CPFE into four types: smoking-related, systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated, occupational- and environmental-related, and idiopathic. These types differ in epidemiologic characteristics, imaging patterns, and disease progression. Consequently, future research is expected to focus on mechanism-driven phenotyping and quantitative imaging analysis, where AI may provide additional value in disease identification, risk stratification, and dynamic prognostic assessment. This review proposes a novel framework for CPFE, integrating etiologic subtyping and a diagnostic algorithm to guide precise management, and highlights AI-powered strategies for future personalized interventions.

title: Digital and artificial intelligence-assisted medication management for older adults with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the results of randomized controlled trials to determine whether medication management approaches based on digital technologies and artificial intelligence/machine learning can indeed bring measurable clinical improvements in older adults with at least one chronic diseases. To identify relevant RCTs, we performed a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, and other databases from their inception through June 30, 2026, for studies of digital and AI/ML-based medication management in older adults with at least one chronic diseases. All stages of study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were conducted independently by two reviewers, applying the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Meta-analytic pooling was conducted via RevMan 5.4. Nineteen RCTs met the inclusion criteria, of which 6 were included in the meta-analysis and 13 in the descriptive synthesis. For medication adherence, three studies reported highly heterogeneous results (I 2 = 97%), and because of this heterogeneity and the small number of studies, the data were not pooled; the individual study estimates ranged from SMD = -0.28-SMD = 1.89. For PIMs, only one study reported a comparable outcome; no pooled estimate was calculated. For hospitalization and mortality, the two included studies used different effect measures (HR and OR) and were therefore presented separately: Blum et al. reported an HR of 0.95 (95% CI 0.77-1.17), and Rieckert et al. reported an OR of 0.88 (95% CI 0.73-1.07). The current body of evidence does not establish clinically meaningful benefits of digital or AI/ML-based medication management on hard endpoints such as hospitalization and mortality among older adults with at least one chronic diseases. For medication adherence, the evidence remains inconclusive and highly heterogeneous, and no reliable pooled estimate could be obtained. Given the pronounced heterogeneity and the limited pool of high-quality RCTs, current evidence is insufficient to establish clinical benefit for the routine implementation of digital or AI/ML-based medication management systems in geriatric care and further rigorously designed studies are warranted. title: Prompting Strategies for Readability Alignment Between User-Generated Ophthalmology Questions and Large Language Model Answers: Comparative Evaluation Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Accessible health communication is essential for effective patient education, yet most medical information remains written at a level above the general population's recommended reading level. Large language models (LLMs) can simplify complex medical information, but it remains unclear whether responses can be automatically adapted to match the linguistic complexity of user-generated questions seeking medical information. To evaluate whether the LLM-generated responses to user-generated ophthalmology questions align with their readability and to compare different prompting strategies for readability control across multiple LLM architectures, including their impact on response quality as well as computational cost and efficiency. A total of 400 user-generated ophthalmology questions collected from public YouTube comments were categorized into 3 readability tiers based on the Flesch Reading Ease Score. A controlled comparative evaluation of responses generated by 4 LLMs (GPT 5.2, Gemini 3, Claude Opus 4.5, and OSS-20b) was performed under 4 prompting conditions: Baseline (no readability control), Formula-Informed Readability Prompt, Semantic Readability Inference, and External Calculator-Guided Prompt. Agreement between question and response readability was assessed using quadratic-weighted Cohen kappa. Response quality was evaluated using BERTScore and LLM-as-a-judge assessments. Computational efficiency was evaluated through token usage, estimated cost per response, and latency. The external calculator-guided strategy produced the strongest alignment in readability across models, achieving the highest agreement (Gemini 3: κ=0.94; GPT 5.2: κ=0.90), while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. Formula-informed prompting showed intermediate performance, whereas semantic inference demonstrated poor agreement due to unreliable readability estimation. High-performing models (GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3) maintained very high factual accuracy (>98%) across strategies, indicating that readability control did not substantially degrade correctness. In contrast, the open-source OSS-20b model showed lower accuracy (83.75%-90%) and greater sensitivity to readability constraints. Semantic similarity remained high across models (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Score [BERTScore] F1>0.87). title: A paradigm shift toward explainable and federated intelligence for brain tumor MRI analysis.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Deep learning techniques in brain tumor analysis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans have improved significantly, but their clinical deployment is limited by models with limited interpretability ('black-box' models) and data privacy limitations. This paper analyses recent literature and aims to explore the intersection of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and Federated Learning (FL). Following the PRISMA protocol, a systematic search was conducted in Scopus on February 24, 2026, covering English-language journal articles and conference proceedings published from January 2020 to February 2026. The search initially identified 767 records, which were screened using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for MRI-based brain tumor studies addressing deep learning, explainability, privacy, or Federated Learning, resulting in 147 initially retained studies for the final screening set. One study was subsequently identified as formally retracted and excluded from the final synthesis, resulting in 146 included studies. The review classifies the literature into five primary research themes in brain tumor analysis: explainability, deep learning frameworks, privacy-preserving learning, advanced architectures (Transformers and Mamba), and multimodal learning. The literature suggests a paradigm shift in brain tumor analysis toward model interpretability using XAI. However, there is a significant knowledge gap in privacy-preserving collaborative learning models. Advanced architectures are proposed to solve brain tumor problems, but there are still limitations in model generalization, computational costs, and clinical reliability.

title: Applications, Technical Characteristics, and Evaluation Approaches of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Nursing: Scoping Review.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] Large language models (LLMs) show great potential for widespread application in the field of nursing; however, their limitations include hallucinations, insufficient domain knowledge, and delays in updating evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), by combining external knowledge retrieval with text generation, holds promise for optimizing model outputs. However, current evidence on the use of RAG in nursing remains fragmented and has not been systematically synthesized. This scoping review aims to map the applications of RAG in the nursing field, identify current research characteristics and gaps, and provide a foundational evidence base to inform future research and development of intelligent tools for nursing practice. This study adopted the Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and followed PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting standards. We systematically searched 9 databases-PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, VIP Database, Wanfang Database, and Sinomed-from inception to September 2026. Backward and forward citation searches were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Eligible publications were restricted to those in English or Chinese during study selection. Two independent reviewers completed study screening and data extraction, and descriptive synthesis was performed for all eligible records. A total of 28 studies published between 2024 and 2026 were included. The application of RAG in nursing primarily focused on 4 scenarios: patient education (n=9), nursing informatics (n=8), clinical decision support (n=7), and nursing education (n=4). The base LLMs included the GPT series, LLaMA, ChatGLM, and Doubao, among others, while the knowledge bases primarily integrated literature, clinical guidelines, institutional resources, and clinical data. Most studies relied on dense retrieval, while some incorporated hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, and reranking to achieve optimization. Generation and task-output evaluations were reported in 27 studies, whereas retrieval evaluation, safety and reliability evaluations, and implementation or outcome evaluations were less frequently reported. Only 4 studies were conducted in real-world clinical settings. Overall, RAG demonstrated potential to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-generated outputs in specific nursing tasks; however, most studies validated only in simu

title: Machine learning for RNA-small molecule interactions: methodologies, evaluation, and future directions.
desc: [Briefings in bioinformatics] RNA is emerging as a compelling therapeutic target due to its rich structural diversity and central involvement in gene regulation, splicing, translation, and cellular signaling. Alongside advances in structural biology, computational approaches, especially machine learning and deep learning, have transformed the systematic analysis of RNA-small molecule interactions. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of computational methods for RNA-small molecule interaction prediction, with a particular emphasis on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and binding pose prediction. We first summarize the data resources commonly used to support these tasks and outline molecular representations that capture RNA structural features and the chemical properties of small molecules. We then review a spectrum of computational approaches for the above three tasks, ranging from statistical methods and traditional machine learning to deep learning. We further evaluate representative methods for each task, providing insights into their respective strengths and limitations. Finally, we highlight open challenges in current research on RNA-small molecule interactions, including limited data availability, the black-box nature of the models, and the growing need for generative modeling. We discuss emerging directions such as data augmentation, model interpretability, and RNA-targeted small-molecule design as promising pathways to address these challenges and advance rational RNA-targeted drug discovery.

title: Characterization of local linearity in deep learning CT denoising networks.
desc: [Medical physics] Deep learning algorithms for image processing have been proposed for a wide range of applications. In particular, deep learning CT denoising has demonstrated superior ability to reduce noise compared to conventional methods. However, the nonlinear nature of these algorithms makes it difficult to inspect and visualize how the model accomplishes the denoising task. We propose a local linearization approach to characterize and analyze the behavior of deep learning algorithms. Example analysis was performed for a classic denoising architecture with convolutional neural network and ReLU activation functions, and was extended to GELU activation and a transformer-based architecture. We defined strictly local linear regions as the input space over which the activation patterns of all ReLU activation functions are the same. The extent of these regions was investigated by perturbing clinically relevant features of a lung lesion. We further defined approximately local linear regions as the input space where Jacobians are similar and linear approximation results in small error. We developed an algorithm to partition input space over a range of lesion and background features into approximately local linear regions, and separately quantified the contribution of the noise realization and anatomical background to this approximation error. The behavior of networks trained with different levels of denoising, as well as alternative architectures, was compared. The extent of strictly local linear regions was found to be very small. Perturbations on the scale of 10 - 8 mm - 1 were enough to push the network to a neighboring strictly local linear region. However, the Jacobians over a large number of strictly local linear regions were found to be highly similar, which suggests that the network behaves approximately as a piecewise linear system. The partitioning algorithm identified a small number of approximately local linear regions within input spaces characterized by clinically relevant features; this number was similar for the GELU variant but increased for networks trained with more aggressive noise reduction and for a transformer-based architecture, while Jacobians transferred across anatomical backgrounds also increased approximation error. The local linearity analysis framework can be a useful tool for elucidating the behavior of neural networks that are traditionally considered as "black-boxes." title: Biomaterial Platforms for Spatiotemporal Control of mRNA Delivery in Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine: Design Rules, Therapeutic Applications, and Translational Roadmap.
source: PubMed · Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany)
desc: [Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany)] Messenger RNA (mRNA) enables transient, non-integrating, and programmable protein expression, yet its regenerative potential is constrained by extracellular instability, inefficient cytosolic delivery, rapid tissue clearance, innate immune activation, and poor alignment between expression kinetics and healing programs. Biomaterial platforms address these barriers by integrating molecular protection and intracellular delivery with local retention, controlled release, biophysical support, and microenvironmental regulation. This Review critically examines nanoscale carriers, macroscale depots and scaffolds, and hierarchical nano-in-matrix and stimulus-responsive systems for spatiotemporally controlled mRNA delivery. We propose a cargo-target-timing framework linking mRNA chemistry and material properties to delivery, expression, immune responses, and tissue repair. Evidence across musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, neural, cutaneous, and visceral tissues is assessed to identify candidate expression profiles, their biological rationale, and the comparative studies needed to define therapeutic windows. Critical quality attributes, longitudinal monitoring, cross-study comparability, manufacturing, storage, dosing, safety, clinically relevant models, and regulatory positioning are evaluated. Finally, a stage-gated translational roadmap and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled, adaptive, and personalized design strategies are presented. By integrating structure-property relationships with tissue-specific therapeutic windows and product-development requirements, this Review establishes actionable principles for advancing mRNA-biomaterial systems toward regenerative products.

title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
desc: [World journal of urology] To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI. 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance. Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

title: RCIRNet: Rotator Cuff Injury Recognition Using Wearable IMU Signals With Cross-Attention.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
desc: [IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society] Rotator cuff injury (RCI) is a common cause of shoulder dysfunction, often accompanied by pain, restricted mobility, and reduced quality of life. Conventional imaging-based diagnostic approaches are effective for structural assessment but are often costly, time-consuming, and difficult to apply in large-scale screening or repeated follow-up. In this study, we propose the RCI recognition network (RCIRNet), a lightweight deep learning model for automated RCI recognition using upper-limb kinematic data collected from wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs). RCIRNet extracts temporal motion features with one-dimensional convolutional layers and introduces a channel-sequence cross-attention (CSCA) module to emphasize informative sensor channels and discriminative movement phases. Multi-segment acceleration signals from the upper thoracic spine, upper arm, and forearm during shoulder abduction are used to distinguish RCI from non-RCI conditions, including adhesive capsulitis and shoulders without dysfunction. Model performance is evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RCIRNet achieves an accuracy of 88.8%, an F1-score of 88.9%, and an AUC of 0.932, outperforming traditional machine-learning models as well as BiLSTM and Transformer Encoder baselines. These results suggest that IMU-based deep learning with channel-sequence attention provides a promising auxiliary tool for low-cost and non-invasive RCI screening.

title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
desc: [iScience] Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with static microenvironment analysis to identify enzyme variants compatible with biomimetic cofactors. Applied to P450BM3, a widely used biocatalyst for chiral synthesis and pharmaceutical precursor production, HelixWings identified a variant with a 404% improvement in catalytic efficiency toward cytochrome c under NMNH-supported conditions. The platform was further validated with CYP116B46, achieving a 217% improvement in NMNH utilization efficiency. HelixWings reduced screening time by 23-fold compared with rational design.

title: Sensor-integrated industrial exoskeletons for ergonomic risk reduction: a systematic review of biomechanical outcomes and intelligent control systems.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology
desc: [Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology] Industrial exoskeletons with integrated sensors are emerging as a technology for monitoring biomechanical exposure and supporting the prevention of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in industrial environments. This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, retrieving 106 studies published between 2021 and 2026 from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 and R-Studio version 2026.01.2+418 were used for bibliometric and descriptive analyses. The review provides a qualitative synthesis supported by descriptive quantitative reporting of the extracted outcomes. The evidence indicated a technological shift from passive devices toward intelligent exoskeletons integrating surface electromyography, inertial measurement units, machine vision, physiological sensors, and artificial intelligence. Individual studies reported maximum reductions of 68.2% in muscle activity, 34% in spinal compression, and up to 60% in muscle fatigue, alongside productivity improvements of up to 59.5%. Machine learning approaches achieved an ROC of 0.985, automated assessment accuracies of 98.5%, and posture estimation with an ICC of 0.967. However, these values were not pooled estimates and varied across study designs, sensor configurations, tasks, and assessment protocols. The evidence remains constrained by small sample sizes, sensor drift, interoperability limitations, and insufficient long-term validation in real-world industrial environments. Sensor-integrated exoskeletons show potential for ergonomic monitoring and risk reduction, but their effectiveness and industrial generalizability require further validation through standardized, interoperable, and longitudinal field studies.

title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants' cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling.
desc: [iScience] Reliably estimating cerebral maturation in preterm newborns is crucial for early identification of atypical neurodevelopment. We developed a deep-learning framework using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict postmenstrual age (PMA) from spontaneous neural activity in EEG recordings of 165 healthy preterm infants (28-38 weeks PMA). The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks, with 73.9% of prediction errors within one week. To identify key neurophysiological drivers, we systematically manipulated signal components. Results showed that removing low-frequency activity ( 12 Hz) had minimal impact. Our results demonstrate that maturation signatures are primarily driven by slow-wave dynamics and their hierarchical coupling with faster oscillations, which are fundamental hallmarks of early neurodevelopment.

title: CasanovoGUI: A Cross-Platform Desktop Application for Deep Learning-Based De Novo Peptide Sequencing with Casanovo.
desc: [Journal of proteome research] De novo peptide sequencing detects peptides directly from tandem mass spectra without a protein sequence database, and deep learning has substantially advanced its performance. Casanovo, one such widely used model, is distributed as a Python command-line program. Consequently, installation, GPU and dependency configuration, and manual parametrization can be challenging for many bench scientists and are a recurring source of errors. Interpreting and validating the resulting predictions poses a further challenge. We present CasanovoGUI, an open-source Java-based desktop application that makes all of Casanovo's main analysis functions available through a point-and-click interface on Windows, macOS, and Linux. On first use, CasanovoGUI automatically installs a private Python environment and Casanovo with a GPU-matched build, requiring no prior software setup. The GUI provides access to Casanovo's analysis functions and configuration parameters, streams live progress, and integrates results interpretation: annotated spectra with per-residue confidence scores in the PDV viewer and mismatch-tolerant mapping of de novo peptides back to a reference proteome. CasanovoGUI is available at https://github.com/Noble-Lab/CasanovoGUI.
